title: The Most Boring Party

pre.en: Who was the woman by the snacks?
pre.zh: 零食桌旁的那个女人是谁？

intro: 一篇新概念式的小故事：「我」被同事拉去一个谁都不认识的生日派对，只想早点回家，却在零食桌旁遇到一个看起来同样无聊的人。读的时候留意 must、can't、could：在陌生的场合，人会不停地猜别人是谁、在想什么——猜得对不对，结尾见分晓。

sentences.en: So, last year my colleague Marcus invited me to a birthday party.
sentences.zh: 去年，同事 Marcus 叫我去参加一个生日派对。

sentences.en: I nearly stayed in.
sentences.zh: 我差点就窝在家里不去了。

sentences.en: I've never enjoyed parties where I don't know anyone.
sentences.zh: 一个人都不认识的派对，我向来不喜欢。

sentences.en: I got there after an hour in rush-hour traffic.
sentences.zh: 晚高峰堵了一个小时，我才到。

sentences.en: Marcus said hello and then vanished into the kitchen.
sentences.zh: Marcus 跟我打了声招呼，转身就钻进厨房不见了。

sentences.en: I tried to make small talk, but I couldn't keep up with all the in-jokes.
sentences.zh: 我想跟人寒暄几句，可他们那些内部梗，我一个都接不上。

sentences.en: After ten minutes, I felt left out.
sentences.zh: 才过了十分钟，我就觉得自己被晾在一边了。

sentences.en: Honestly, I couldn't wait to go home.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我恨不得马上回家。

sentences.en: I ended up standing by the snacks, where a woman was eating crisps and checking her phone.
sentences.zh: 最后我晃到了零食桌旁，那儿有个女人正一边吃薯片一边看手机。

sentences.en: She must be bored too, I thought.
sentences.zh: 她肯定也觉得没劲，我心想。

sentences.en: She can't know anyone here either.
sentences.zh: 她在这儿肯定也一个人都不认识。

sentences.en: So I took a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 于是我深吸了一口气。

sentences.en: Then I tried to break the ice: "Have you ever heard worse music?"
sentences.zh: 然后找了个话头：「你听过比这更难听的音乐吗？」

sentences.en: To my surprise, she laughed.
sentences.zh: 没想到，她笑了。

sentences.en: "Never," she said, and pointed at an old man in an armchair.
sentences.zh: 「从来没有，」她说着，指了指扶手椅里的一位老先生。

sentences.en: He was fast asleep and snoring.
sentences.zh: 他睡得正香，还打着呼噜。

sentences.en: "Well, he must be the happiest guest here."
sentences.zh: 「嗯，他肯定是这儿最开心的客人。」

sentences.en: Actually, we had a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 其实，我们俩有很多共同点。

sentences.en: We both hated dancing, and we both loved spicy food.
sentences.zh: 都讨厌跳舞，都爱吃辣。

sentences.en: I got along with her straight away.
sentences.zh: 我跟她一下子就聊得来。

sentences.en: "Where's the birthday girl, anyway?" I asked.
sentences.zh: 「对了，寿星在哪儿呢？」我问。

sentences.en: "Oh, she could be anywhere," she said with a grin.
sentences.zh: 「哦，那可说不好，哪儿都有可能，」她咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: We were still laughing when the lights went off and Marcus came in with a cake.
sentences.zh: 我们还在笑，灯突然灭了，Marcus 端着蛋糕走了进来。

sentences.en: Everyone sang "Happy birthday, dear Anna" and turned to look at us.
sentences.zh: 大家唱起「祝亲爱的 Anna 生日快乐」，齐刷刷地转过头来看我们。

sentences.en: It turned out I'd spent an hour complaining to the birthday girl.
sentences.zh: 原来，我对着寿星本人吐槽了整整一个小时。

sentences.en: "You're right, though," she laughed.
sentences.zh: 「不过你说得没错，」她笑着说，

sentences.en: "It's my party, and I'm bored too."
sentences.zh: 「这是我的派对，我也觉得没劲。」

sentences.en: So we left early and went out for spicy noodles.
sentences.zh: 于是我们提前溜了，出去吃了碗辣面。

sentences.en: Last month we celebrated her birthday again, at the same noodle place.
sentences.zh: 上个月，我们又给她过了一次生日，还是在那家面馆。

cards.note: to stay at home and not go out
the busy time of day when most people are travelling to or from work
比 disappear 更突然，像凭空不见了一样；vanish into + 地方：一下钻进某处不见了。
to have a polite conversation about unimportant things, especially with people you don't know well
cards.tip: small talk 是不可数名词，不说 a small talk；「闲聊」的动词用 make，不用 say 或 do。
cards.example: I'm not good at making small talk with clients before a meeting starts.

cards.note: to move or make progress at the same speed as someone or something
只有一群熟人才听得懂的梗；美式英语说 inside joke。

cards.zh: 觉得被冷落；觉得被排除在外
cards.note: to feel that you are not included in a group or an activity
cards.tip: left out 是「被落下」的意思，前面用 feel 或 be；「把某人晾在一边」是 leave sb out：Don't leave her out.
cards.example: New team members often feel left out when everyone talks about old projects.

cards.note: to be very excited about something and want it to happen soon
cards.tip: 后面接动词原形。这里是 couldn't wait to go home「巴不得马上回家」——同一个说法，既能说盼着的好事，也能说想逃离的场合。
cards.example: I can't wait to see the new office on Monday.

cards.note: to be in a place or situation in the end, often without planning it
英式英语里 crisps 是薯片，chips 是炸薯条；美式英语里薯片才叫 chips。

cards.zh: 深吸一口气（给自己壮胆、让自己镇定）
cards.note: to breathe in a lot of air, especially to calm yourself before something difficult
cards.tip: 常放在做难事之前，后面接 and + 动作。breath /breθ/ 是名词，动词是 breathe /briːð/，别拼混。
cards.example: I took a deep breath and pressed Send.

cards.zh: 打破沉默；（跟陌生人）打开话匣子
cards.note: to say or do something that helps people relax when they meet for the first time
cards.tip: ice 前面一定带 the。主语也可以是一件事：A joke about the weather broke the ice.
cards.example: Our manager always breaks the ice with a silly question at the start of a workshop.

cards.note: used to say that something was not what you expected
cards.tip: 一般放句首，后面加逗号；换人称就换物主代词：to her surprise、to our surprise。介词只能用 to，不说 for my surprise。
cards.example: To my surprise, the client liked our first design.

cards.note: 坐在扶手椅里用 in：sit in an armchair；坐在普通椅子上用 on：sit on a chair。
to share many of the same interests, opinions or experiences
cards.tip: 跟谁有共同点用 with：I have a lot in common with her。反过来是 have nothing in common。不说 have many common points。
cards.example: My new colleague and I have a lot in common — we both hate long meetings.

cards.note: to have a friendly relationship with someone
cards.tip: 英式英语也常说 get on with。后面不跟人时去掉 with：We got along straight away.
cards.example: I get along with my new manager much better than I expected.

cards.note: 英式口语，和 right away、immediately 意思一样，放在句末。
不管多大年纪都可以这么叫，带点亲昵；男的说 birthday boy。
比 smile 笑得更开，常带点得意或调皮；也能当动词：She grinned at me.
to happen in a way you did not expect, or to be discovered to be true
cards.tip: It turned out (that) + 句子，that 口语里常省略，就像这句；也可以说 sb turned out to be …。
cards.example: The urgent bug turned out to be a typo.
